samples.summary: PDF link annotation writes an attacker-controlled href unescaped into a PDF literal string — arbitrary PDF object injection into every exported PDF
samples.evidence: `addLinkAnnotation` builds the action dict with `URI: PDFString.of(uri)` (pdf-painter.ts:896) from the raw `style.href` (gate at pdf-painter.ts:851). pdf-lib's `PDFString` serialises as `(` + value + `)` with no escaping of `)` or `\`, and `isSafeUrl` happily accepts `https://example.com/)` — `new URL()` allows parentheses in a path and only the protocol is checked. Attack: an attacker gets an href such as `https://x/)/Type/Action/S/JavaScript/JS(app.alert(1))>>` into the model — trivially, since HTML paste copies `<a href>` verbatim with no validation (`packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:597-601`) and a collaborator's CRDT write is unchecked — then any user who exports the document to PDF produces a file whose Link annotation dictionary contains attacker-authored PDF syntax (e.g. a /JavaScript or /Launch action, or a rewritten /URI), which fires when a third party opens the PDF in a viewer that honours it. This change deliberately documents the defect as issue #988 and leaves it in place (comment added at pdf-painter.ts:848-850); the underlying line is pre-existing, but it is a live injection and this PR is what pins and tests this gate.

samples.summary: resolvePageSetup does not enforce MIN_CONTENT_PX for a sub-pixel page, so a hostile CRDT/API page setup can hang or OOM every replica during pagination
samples.evidence: `fitMargins` short-circuits at `if (total === 0) return [0, 0]` (types.ts:795) and otherwise clamps `scale` to 0, so for a stored `paperSize.height` below `MIN_CONTENT_PX` the resolver returns a content box far below the floor its own docstring promises (`usableSize` accepts *any* finite positive number, types.ts ~772). That geometry is remotely settable: `readPageSetup` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:530-543 turns whatever a collaborator wrote into `Number(...)`, and the deliberate write-path guard (`assertUsablePageSetup`) is never on that path. With `contentHeight = 1e-6`, `paginateLayout`'s table row-split loop `while (consumed < rowHeight)` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:116-138) advances by `min(remaining, pageAvail)` = 1e-6 per iteration and calls `startNewPage()` each time, so a single ordinary table row (~20 px) costs ~2e7 iterations and ~2e7 page objects — a hang/OOM in the editor of every collaborator who opens the document, and in PDF/DOCX export. This directly contradicts the new docstring's claim that clamping exists so 'a remote peer must not be able to make this replica's document un-openable' (types.ts ~800-812).

samples.summary: Read-only (share-link viewer) mode remains bypassable through getStore()/getDoc(); the new partial guard makes the handle read as guarded while server-side enforcement is off by default
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` drops the write when `readOnly` (editor.ts:2904) and the proxy replaces only `setPageSetup` (editor.ts:2915); every other DocStore mutator forwards untouched, and `getDoc()` returns a Doc writing straight to the unwrapped store. The change ships a test that asserts the bypass still works — `editor.getStore().insertText('b1', 5, '!!')` succeeds in read-only (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts, '#989' test). The comment claims the server is the authoritative boundary, but that boundary is opt-in: `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` defaults to false (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88, README:111), and in shadow mode the webhook returns allow for a viewer's `rw` attribute (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:97-105). So in a default deployment a share-link *viewer* who runs one line of JS (or drives the Yorkie client with the token they already hold) can write to a document they only have read access to. Pre-existing and tracked as #989, but this PR's half-guard is exactly the 'added-but-bypassable gate that reads as covered' pattern.

samples.summary: assertUsablePageSetup is bypassable on the very handle it guards — setDocument/replaceDocument write pageSetup unvalidated, and the proxy leaves getPrototypeOf untrapped
samples.evidence: The proxy intercepts only `prop === 'setPageSetup'` (editor.ts:2915) and forwards everything else. `DocStore.setDocument` / `replaceDocument` persist a whole `Document` including `pageSetup` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:766 and :779; MemDocStore likewise), so `editor.getStore().setDocument({...doc, pageSetup: closedBox})` writes geometry the assert exists to refuse into the CRDT for every collaborator — and neither method is in `MUTATING_METHODS`, so it works in read-only too. `getPrototypeOf` is also untrapped, so `Object.getPrototypeOf(store).setPageSetup.call(store, bad)` reaches the raw setter. Impact is bounded by the read-side clamp in `resolvePageSetup`, but the docstring's claim that 'there is no second way to write a page setup' is not true of the handle it is written on.

samples.summary: escapeMarkdownText does not escape block-level Markdown constructs, so attacker-controlled run text can forge headings/lists/rules in the exported .md
samples.evidence: `escapeMarkdownText` escapes only `\ * _ [ ] ` ~ <` (markdown.ts:478-482). `blockToMarkdown` emits a paragraph's text at the start of a line verbatim (markdown.ts:112-113), so a run whose text begins with `# `, `- `, `> `, `1. ` or `---` — content that arrives unvalidated from HTML/JSON paste, DOCX import or a collaborator's CRDT write — renders as a heading, list item, blockquote or thematic break in the exported file. Not XSS (`<` is escaped and the newline fold at markdown.ts:480 closes the multi-line case), but it lets an attacker forge document structure in a `.md` that a human or a downstream automated consumer reads as authoritative. The new test 'keeps a blank line in a text run from forging a new block' asserts the folded output `intro  # Forged heading`, i.e. the line-start case is untested and unhandled.

samples.summary: URI_CHARS admits U+0080–U+FFFF wholesale, so bidi overrides and zero-width characters survive into emitted link destinations
samples.evidence: `URI_CHARS` (markdown.ts:282) allows every non-ASCII code unit so that e.g. `/uploads/한글.png` round-trips, and `UNEMITTABLE_URL_CHARS` only removes `\s` plus C0/C1. U+200B/U+200D/U+00AD/U+202A–U+202E therefore pass `isLiteralDestination` and are written into the destination (and, via `escapeMarkdownText`, into the link text). No scheme bypass follows — a URL parser does not fold these into ASCII — but a bidi override in a destination or link text is a display-spoofing ('Trojan Source') vector for whatever renders the exported Markdown.

samples.summary: safeFilename, now extended to .md/.txt, strips only a fixed punctuation set — control characters, bidi overrides and a leading dot survive into the download filename
samples.evidence: `safeFilename` replaces only `[\\/:*?"<>|]+` (export-utils.ts:110) and is now reached by two more formats via `exportMarkdownAndDownload` / `exportTextAndDownload`. A document title carrying U+202E or C0 characters is passed to `a.download` (export-utils.ts:65), giving an extension-spoofing filename; a title beginning with `.` yields a dotfile. Pre-existing and identical for the already-shipped `.pdf`/`.docx`, and the task notes record it as a known limitation, so this is hardening only.

finding.summary: PDF link annotation writes an attacker-controlled href unescaped into a PDF literal string — arbitrary PDF object injection into every exported PDF
finding.evidence: `addLinkAnnotation` builds the action dict with `URI: PDFString.of(uri)` (pdf-painter.ts:896) from the raw `style.href` (gate at pdf-painter.ts:851). pdf-lib's `PDFString` serialises as `(` + value + `)` with no escaping of `)` or `\`, and `isSafeUrl` happily accepts `https://example.com/)` — `new URL()` allows parentheses in a path and only the protocol is checked. Attack: an attacker gets an href such as `https://x/)/Type/Action/S/JavaScript/JS(app.alert(1))>>` into the model — trivially, since HTML paste copies `<a href>` verbatim with no validation (`packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:597-601`) and a collaborator's CRDT write is unchecked — then any user who exports the document to PDF produces a file whose Link annotation dictionary contains attacker-authored PDF syntax (e.g. a /JavaScript or /Launch action, or a rewritten /URI), which fires when a third party opens the PDF in a viewer that honours it. This change deliberately documents the defect as issue #988 and leaves it in place (comment added at pdf-painter.ts:848-850); the underlying line is pre-existing, but it is a live injection and this PR is what pins and tests this gate.

verdict.reason: The finding checks out at every step. pdf-painter.ts:851 gates on isSafeUrl but pdf-painter.ts:856 then passes the RAW style.href to addLinkAnnotation, which writes it via PDFString.of at pdf-painter.ts:896. isSafeUrl (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31) is only `new URL()` + a protocol allowlist; parentheses are legal in a URL path and are not percent-encoded by the WHATWG parser, so `https://x/)/Type/Action/S/JavaScript/JS(app.alert(1))>>` passes the gate. pdf-lib is pinned at ^1.17.1 (packages/docs/package.json:59), whose PDFString.of emits `(` + value + `)` with no escaping of `)` or `\` — the repo's own lessons file (docs/tasks/archive/2026/04/20260430-pdf-export-lessons.md:35-36) documents PDFString's rawness for titles. So the `)` closes the literal string early and the remainder becomes attacker-authored dictionary syntax inside the Link annotation's action dict (/JavaScript, /Launch, rewritten /URI). The taint source is real and unvalidated: clipboard.ts:597-601 copies `<a href>` verbatim into style.href (also clipboard.ts:148-149 for the internal JSON path); no sanitizer sits between model and painter. Notably the Markdown serializer DOES escape this exact class (serialize/markdown.ts:500-516 escapeMarkdownHref escapes parens), showing the PDF path is the unguarded one. The in-code comment (pdf-painter.ts:848-850) and test note (test/export/pdf-exporter.test.ts:474-476) explicitly acknowledge the defect and defer it to issue #988, and the pinned tests (518-532) only cover scheme/relative cases, so no test would catch a `)` payload. Deliberate deferral does not make the vulnerability unreal or unreachable; injection with a broken output-encoding boundary is squarely in the Security lens and critical in impact.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end. usableSize (types.ts:766-770) accepts any finite positive paper dimension with no minimum, and fitMargins (types.ts:784-798) clamps scale to 0 for a sub-pixel extent, so resolvePageSetup returns a content box of ~1e-6 — below the MIN_CONTENT_PX=1 floor its docstring (types.ts:820-824) promises. That geometry is remotely settable: readPageSetup (yorkie-doc-store.ts:530-543) coerces a collaborator's CRDT values with Number(...) and no bounds, and getPageSetup (yorkie-doc-store.ts:661-666) / getDocument (:604-606) pass them to resolvePageSetup; the write-path guard assertUsablePageSetup (editor.ts:976-1013) is not on that path and itself only requires width/height > 0. The editor calls resolvePageSetup -> paginateLayout every recompute (editor.ts:1392,1407). With contentHeight ~1e-6 the table row-split loop (pagination.ts:116-138) advances by min(remaining, pageAvail) = 1e-6 per iteration — startNewPage() resets currentY to 0 (:71) so pageAvail never grows — and pushes a LayoutPage each pass, so one ~20px row costs ~2e7 iterations/page objects: a hang/OOM for every collaborator opening the doc and for PDF/DOCX export. Additional unvalidated entry points: docx-parser.ts:341-347 and pdf-exporter.ts:101. No guard elsewhere clamps minimum page size; the finding is real and in-lane (untrusted input handling / remotely triggered availability failure that defeats the stated threat-model guarantee).

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. The proxy at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2913-2929 traps only `setPageSetup` (line 2915) and binds all other DocStore members straight to the real store; `readOnly` is honored solely inside `guardedSetPageSetup` (line 2904), and `getDoc()` (line 2933) returns the unwrapped Doc. The repo ships a test that pins the bypass as working: `editor.getStore().insertText('b1', 5, '!!')` in read-only mode asserts 'hello!! world' (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:351-359). The claimed authoritative boundary is opt-in: YorkieAuthController sets `enforce` only when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true' (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88) and in shadow mode returns ALLOW for every deny decision (97-105), with README:111 documenting false as the default — so the viewer-role check `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true` (line 200) is not enforced by default. The write also reaches the server rather than staying local: SharedDocsLayout mounts DocsView (shared-document.tsx:277-306), which builds a live `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` and passes it to `initialize(..., readOnly)` (docs-view.tsx:324-327). So a share-link viewer running one line of JS mutates the CRDT for all collaborators. This is in-lane (weakened/bypassable role gate) and the guard reads as covering the handle while covering one method; no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.

finding.summary: PDF injection: attacker-controlled `style.href` is written into a PDF literal string via `PDFString.of()`, which escapes neither `(`/`)` nor `\`
finding.evidence:
`addLinkAnnotation` builds `A: ctx.obj({ Type: 'Action', S: 'URI', URI: PDFString.of(uri) })` (pdf-painter.ts:893-897) with `uri === style.href` verbatim (pdf-painter.ts:856). pdf-lib ^1.17.1 (`packages/docs/package.json:59`) serialises `PDFString` as `(` + raw bytes + `)` (`copyBytesInto` writes `CharCodes.LeftParen`, the raw string, `CharCodes.RightParen`) with no escaping of `(`, `)` or `\` — this is a documented pdf-lib caveat; `PDFHexString` is the escaping-safe alternative, and this repo already uses `PDFHexString.fromText` for metadata at pdf-exporter.ts:240.

The gate on line 851 is `isSafeUrl(style.href)`, which only checks `new URL(href).protocol` against `['http:','https:','mailto:','tel:']`. Parentheses and backslashes are perfectly legal in an http(s) path, so `new URL('https://x/)>>/S/JavaScript/JS(app.alert(1)')` parses fine and returns protocol `https:` — the gate passes.

Attack: an attacker sets an inline's `href` to e.g. `https://x/) /S /JavaScript /JS (app.alert(1)` . Reachable vectors, none of which validate the value on the way in: (a) HTML paste — `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:597-600` does `const href = el.getAttribute('href'); if (href) style.href = href;` with no filtering, so copying from an attacker-controlled page is enough; (b) a collaborator with editor rights writing the CRDT; (c) the authenticated API `PUT /api/v1/.../content`, whose `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:424-447) validates only that `inline.style` is an object. A victim then uses Export → PDF. The emitted object becomes `<< /Type /Action /S /URI /URI (https://x/) /S /JavaScript /JS (app.alert(1)) >>`: the `/URI` string closes at the first `)` and the remainder is parsed as additional PDF dictionary entries in the annotation's action, letting an attacker override the action type (`/S /JavaScript`, `/S /Launch`) or otherwise inject arbitrary PDF syntax that the exporter never intended. At minimum this is structural PDF inject

verdict.reason: All load-bearing claims check out in this tree. pdf-painter.ts:851 gates on isSafeUrl(style.href), then pdf-painter.ts:856 passes the raw style.href to addLinkAnnotation, which at pdf-painter.ts:896 writes it as PDFString.of(uri) inside the annotation's action dictionary. isSafeUrl (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31) only parses the URL and compares url.protocol against ['http:','https:','mailto:','tel:'] — it returns a boolean and constrains nothing about '(', ')' or '\', all of which are legal in an http(s) path/query, and the caller writes the original string rather than the parsed one. pdf-lib ^1.17.1 (packages/docs/package.json:59) serialises PDFString as literal '(' + raw bytes + ')' with no escaping; the repo's own use of the escaping-safe PDFHexString.fromText for metadata (pdf-exporter.ts:238-240) confirms the asymmetry. Untrusted ingress is real and unfiltered: clipboard.ts:597-600 and :699-702 assign el.getAttribute('href') straight into style.href from pasted HTML, and clipboard.ts:148-149 accepts any string href on deserialization. Grep over packages/docs/src/export shows no sanitization between ingress and sink. The comment at pdf-painter.ts:848-850 acknowledging a deferred defect (issue #988, validate-vs-write) is an admission, not a guard. Result is attacker-controlled PDF syntax injected into the /A action dict (e.g. closing the /URI string and appending /S /JavaScript or /S /Launch) — injection lane, blocking. Caveat noted transparently: node_modules is absent so pdf-lib's PDFString.copyBytesInto could not be read in-tree; that single link rests on the library's known behaviour, which the repo's own PDFHexString usage corroborates.
